title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: deterministic BSGS, Jacobian walks with blocked Montgomery normalisation and a 128-bit-counter radix sort

claims.statement: For uniform s in [1,r) with T=[s]P0 in the protected BLS12-381 G1 subgroup, using only the public A_1=T and the deterministic baby-step/giant-step construction in proof.md (m=h=ceil(sqrt(r))=228988810152649578064853576960394133504, Jacobian mixed-addition walks charged at 11M each, blocked Montgomery batch inversion of 2^16 Z-coordinates for the affine normalisation, 24-digit radix sort on the 381-bit x key with 128-bit multiword counters, and a single linear merge), the attack recovers s and succeeds with probability 1, hence at least 0.39 over uniform production challenges and fresh algorithm coins, using at most 2^130.533720 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, normalisation, sorting, merge, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^135.013508 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^129.533720 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. W(n) equals this bound for every n>=1 and the score is evaluated at n=2^20. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum step or heuristic assumption; the exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting control, not a claim of novelty or of a practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the submitted construction (Jacobian walks, sort-by-x, merge scan, infinity and +- branches, verification) on small Weierstrass groups for every s in 1..r-1. This does not establish production curve behaviour, memory bounds or operation costs.
